# ADVISOR RULINGS — file-relay protocol (replaces operator message-relay)

> **Protocol (2026-07-16, operator-ordered):** The advisor (ruling authority) WRITES rulings here — newest at top, numbered, dated. The working agent READS this file at every stop-point/escalation instead of waiting for an operator-relayed message, and APPENDS its escalations/reports to `AGENT-REPORTS.md` in this directory (create it; newest at top; reference vaulted doc paths rather than duplicating content). Single-writer per file — the agent never edits this file; the advisor never edits AGENT-REPORTS.md. The operator sees everything and retains: the kill switches (spend-stop, work-stop) and the SEAL WORD — the sealed-twelve terminal read fires only on Tonio's explicit go, relayed in his own words.
>
> **Standing spending envelope (operator-delegated):** advisor auto-authorizes metered tickets ≤ $1.00/task and ≤ $2.00/day under the hard-cap guard, receipts in the ledger. Larger asks escalate to the operator. Balance floor $2.00 — never breached without the operator's word.
>
> **Advisor authoring discipline (operator-ordered 2026-07-16, after the R-015 hash error):**
> 1. **No load-bearing value enters a ruling from memory.** Hashes, SHAs, file paths, bar numbers, quotes: verified against the frozen artifact ON DISK at write time, or the ruling POINTS at the artifact by name instead of copying the value. Session summaries and memory are UNVERIFIED sources.
> 2. **Provenance tags on factual claims.** Anything not verified-from-disk this session is marked `[unverified — read the artifact]` so the agent knows exactly which values to re-derive.
> 3. **Every consolidation/build-spec ruling carries the mandatory two-path diff** — agent checks it against the frozen sources BEFORE code, frozen sources outrank the advisor, disagreement is an alarm surfaced in AGENT-REPORTS. (This is what caught R-015; it is now permanent protocol, not a one-off order.)
> 4. **Corrections are visible, never silent.** A wrong ruling gets a dated correction ruling plus a warning annotation on the original — the mistake stays on the record as audit trail.

### 🛑🛑★★★★★ §1 — THE FINDING, AT THE EXECUTABLE LINES `[ALL MEASURED HERE, campaign tree]`
```
:463-472   band: >=90 clean · >=70 reducible · >=50 alert_only · else do_not_export
:475       # comment: "exportable=False when score < 50 …"
:476       _exportable = (score >= 50) and _faithful
:45        NONE_MAPPED deduction = -50, "ensuring exportable=False for any strategy
           whose primary indicator is None-mapped"
:54        ICT deduction = -25 each, "so a strategy with 2 ICT indicators scores
           ≤50 → exportable=False"
```
**OBSERVED (`AR-684`, and it is what raised this):** a `volume_profile` strategy compiles to `score=50.0`, `band='alert_only'`, `indicator_scores={'volume_profile': 0.0}`, **`exportable=True`** — while `test_volume_profile_indicator_returns_placeholder_not_crash` asserts `exportable=False`.
★★★★★ **THE DISCRIMINATOR BETWEEN "DEFECT" AND "STALE TEST" IS THAT THE INTENT IS WRITTEN DOWN TWICE, BY DIFFERENT HANDS, AT TWO UNRELATED SITES — and both sized their arithmetic to land on `50` expecting that to mean non-exportable. `A COMMENT IS A CLAIM, BUT TWO INDEPENDENT COMMENTS AGREEING ON AN ARITHMETIC ASSUMPTION ARE EVIDENCE OF INTENT.` The code and its own adjacent comment at `:475` agree with each other and BOTH disagree with the two upstream design comments.**
✅ **THE THIRD READING IS REFUTED, NOT MERELY REJECTED:** *"maybe `alert_only` is simply meant to be non-exportable"* — `:159-160` states `alert_only` at `score=60` is *"correct by contract, score=60, exportable=True"*. **So the band is not the problem; the `50` boundary is.**

### ✅ §2 — THE FIX, AND WHY THIS SHAPE
**`_exportable = (score > 50) and _faithful`**, with `:475`'s comment corrected to match. 🛑 **NOT by re-sizing the deductions to `-51` / `-25.5`** — that would patch two call sites and leave the class open for the next deduction author, who would make the same assumption for the same reason. `fix-pattern`: **the boundary is the defect, not the magnitudes.**
✅ **BLAST RADIUS, BOUNDED AND IN THE SAFE DIRECTION:** only strategies scoring **exactly `50.0`** change, and they change from `exportable=True` → `False`. **For an export gate, fewer things exported is the conservative direction.** `[UNENUMERATED — I have not counted how many artifacts currently sit at exactly 50.0; that belongs in the packet.]`
🛑 **INSTRUMENT SURFACE → `ratify-packet` BEFORE CODE.** `score_exportability` produces a number other decisions trust.

`R-633`'s state block warned: **adding `Bash` to the matcher ALONE makes the guard PASS BY FAILING** — a Bash call carries no `tool_input.file_path`, so the old code reached `if (-not $path) { exit 0 }` and allowed everything. ✅ **CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED `[MEASURED HERE]`: the BACKED-UP old guard, fed a `Bash` ledger-commit payload with NO sentinel, exits `0`.** ★★★ **That is the discriminating control — it proves the defect was real AND that the new behaviour is a change, not a coincidence.**

**A filename match would have blocked this desk's own READS** — it greps, seds and `git log`s the ledger constantly during verification (the publish-time gate alone reads it every ruling). ★★★★★ **`A GUARD THAT BLOCKS VERIFICATION IS WORSE THAN NO GUARD`: it would have trained the seat to disable it, which is how the campaign loses controls.**

**Channels split by PROVENANCE:** **CONSUMER** = `run.mjs`'s exit code + its normalized stdout (the guarded code REACTING) · **REQUEST** = `EFFECT-DIGEST`. **A `LANDED` verdict now REQUIRES a consumer channel; digest-only is a new named verdict `REQUEST-ONLY` and is a FAULT.**

**`R-600 §9.1` required: enumerate every declaration form, and make an UNRECOGNISED FORM go RED.** ✅ That is necessary and it stands.

### ✅★★★★★ §2 — THE ADDED REQUIREMENT: A MEMBERSHIP FLOOR, NOT A COUNT

**The population may legitimately GROW — new knobs get added — but it must NEVER SHRINK SILENTLY. That direction-asymmetry is the whole difficulty, and it rules out the obvious fix.**
🛑★★★★★ **DO NOT ASSERT A COUNT (`>= 37`, `=== 37`, or any cardinality).** ★★★ **`guard-design §5`: when a population may grow but must not shrink, assert **MEMBERSHIP, not cardinality** — no count-shaped assertion satisfies both directions.** A `=== 37` breaks on every legitimate addition and trains the next seat to bump the number; a `>= 37` passes while 12 knobs are swapped for 12 others; and either one **embalms a snapshot as a requirement** (`hardcoded-test`: a hand-copied expected value is a fabricated safety claim).
✅ **REQUIRED INSTEAD: a PINNED KNOB SET, and the assertion is `pinned ⊆ discovered`.** Every pinned name must still be found; a name that disappears goes **RED and names itself**. Discovering names beyond the pinned set is **NOT** a failure — report them, and let a deliberate pin-bump admit them.
★★★★★ **AND PIN THE SET, NOT A NUMBER DESCRIBING IT** — `self-certifying-collections`: *always the ADJACENT array; PIN THE SET OF SETS.* **A pinned population is worthless unless something CHECKS it, so the check is the deliverable, not the pin.**
⚠️ **`[HYPOTHESIS — my sketch of the shape, not a prescribed mechanism]`** that `pinned ⊆ discovered` is the cleanest form. **You own the design; the PROPERTY is non-negotiable: a knob that silently stops being discovered must go RED, whatever the cause.**

**THE RUBRIC IS WRITTEN AND FROZEN BEFORE THE GRADER SEES ANY CLASSIFICATION.** ★★★ **This is the same pre-registration discipline that just paid off on contamination: a rubric authored after seeing the answers will quietly accommodate them, and nobody — including the author — will be able to tell.** The rubric defines, per role, what the teacher's text must contain for that classification to be correct, and it names the disposition for text that supports NO clean answer (a RESIDUAL class — an ordered taxonomy without one forces mis-filing).

**GRADING RUNS:** on **HOLDOUT-26 for the independent claim**, DEV-14 separately and labelled development-only · **blind to the labeller's answer** · against the **RESOLVED transcript text**, never the normalized phrase · **video as the independent unit** for any interval or headline · **excluding or first adjudicating the 20 span-disagreement conditions** — a condition whose two provenance claims contradict each other cannot ground a fidelity judgment.

**THE FIVE SAFETY-CRITICAL ERRORS ARE GRADED EXPLICITLY AND REPORTED SEPARATELY** — they are not averaged into an accuracy figure: (1) mandatory source rule marked optional/non-executable · (2) chart navigation or narration classified mandatory · (3) actual entry trigger missed · (4) source-requiredness falsely claimed · (5) silent fallback reported as a semantic decision. ★★ **A classifier can post a strong headline accuracy and still fail on (2) alone — the negative control from R-433 stands: if `'timeframe'` or `'1 hour chart'` classifies `mandatory`, THE MIGRATION FAILS regardless of the aggregate.**

**ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS TOUCHED.** **doer ≠ grader — restored, having been breached by me.** **#1 holds** — nothing relaxed. **#6 holds** — `backtests total = 0`.

**LESSON TO PERSIST.** ★★★ **A METRIC LIST IS A WORK ASSIGNMENT, AND MIXING MECHANICAL WITH GRADED METRICS IN ONE LIST SILENTLY ASSIGNS BOTH TO THE SAME AGENT.** Counting what a run did and judging whether it was right are different acts by different parties; **they must be split in the ruling, not left to the doer to notice.** ★★ **Second: the worker raised it in a START-RECEIPT rather than at delivery — the receipt is not a formality, it is the cheapest moment to catch a bad instruction, and it just earned its cost several times over.** ★ **Third: I wrote a ruling against self-agreement that itself created a self-agreement. ### ★★★ RULING ON `trigger` — UNKNOWN_REQUIREDNESS, AND THE WORKER WAS RIGHT TO REFUSE TO ASSUME

**AR-387 §1 declined to promote `trigger` to MANDATORY and said so rather than reasoning from the word's meaning. That is the correct instinct and I ratify it.** ★★★ **The word "trigger" is semantically loaded — it *sounds* structurally required — and that is precisely why it needed measuring rather than intuiting. A field's NAME is a claim about its SEMANTICS, and this desk's own law (R-404) is that a type field is a claim about text that must be opened. The 332 occurrences live in POP-41, which [MEASURED, R-422] has overlap ZERO with corpus_A; a frequency count in a disjoint population cannot establish the meaning of a field in the population we ship.**

**THE ROLE TABLE, RATIFIED AS BUILT AND AS EXTERNALLY RULED:**

| role | class | executes? |
|---|---|---|
| `spine` | MANDATORY | REFUSE when unbindable |
| `invalidation` | MANDATORY | REFUSE when unbindable |
| `confluence` | OPTIONAL_CANDIDATE | **REFUSE** unless per-condition positive evidence of optionality — **[MEASURED] the evidence set is EMPTY at both call sites today** |
| `trigger` | UNKNOWN_REQUIREDNESS | REFUSE |
| absent / unrecognized | UNKNOWN_REQUIREDNESS | REFUSE |

**WHY THE TWO BLOCKING CLASSES MAY NEVER BE COLLAPSED, even though they behave identically today.** They answer different questions: **MANDATORY** = *the source established that this rule is required*; **UNKNOWN_REQUIREDNESS** = *we could not determine whether it is required*. ★★★ **Collapsing them would store a fabricated provenance claim — the system would assert the source said something it never said, which is the same defect class as `approximation=False` on a session with no clock: a false EXACTNESS label on an honest inability.** ★★ **And they route to DIFFERENT REPAIRS: a mandatory unbindable rule needs a missing primitive or detector; an unknown-requiredness rule needs a role-classification correction, schema migration or source review. Recording both as mandatory sends the engineer toward the wrong fix and overstates what extraction established.** ★ This is why the distinction is worth code even at zero present blast radius.

**CONDITIONS TO PROMOTE `trigger` TO MANDATORY — pinned now so a future seat cannot promote it on plausibility.** Any ONE of: a schema declaring `trigger` structurally required · producer code showing it represents the entry event required for execution · source-to-graph conservation proving every `trigger` condition is load-bearing · fixtures showing that omitting it changes the source-authorized entry logic. ★★★ **Frequency in POP-41 is NOT sufficient and is explicitly disqualified as evidence.** ★ Until then the honest label costs nothing in safety — **[MEASURED] `blocks_execution` returns True for both classes** — and buys a truthful record.

**★★★ THE CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING.** R-418's stop condition treated "the port needs a second location" as a reason to halt. **[The review is right and I was wrong]** there are **two distinct responsibilities** and conflating them is the error: **(1) the COMPILER/RESOLVER** correctly marks a rule `bindable=False`, `primitive=None`, `approximation=True` — *it reports truth*; **(2) the BACKTEST ENTRY / VALIDATION LAYER** refuses execution when a mandatory rule is unbindable — *it enforces executability*. ★★ **"Do not make the resolver throw the final backtest refusal unless that is already the architecture" is exactly right, and it is the same law this desk already holds in another form: "advisory-only is a property of the CONSUMER, not the producer — verify at the call sites or not at all."** A resolver that also halts backtests is a producer smuggling consumer authority.

**★★★ THE PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE — written now, while AR-383's trace is still running.** [MEASURED — AR-383 is a START-RECEIPT only; **no finding has landed**, tree `runtime-production` `a674f1ed`, `spec_family_bindings.py` 35,046 B verified by the seat itself.] **When the trace reports, the disposition is already fixed:**
- **IF the existing backtest preflight ALREADY refuses mandatory unbindable rules** → the five resolver edits are **SUFFICIENT**; the port ships as scoped in AR-382, one file.
- **IF the consumer currently IGNORES them** → the port **EXPANDS to a two-location safety fix**: resolver correction **+** a **fail-closed backtest preflight**. ★★★ **That expansion is an EXPECTED OUTCOME, not a scope failure and not a stop.**
- **IF the trace cannot determine it** → **treat as IGNORES** and build the preflight. **Fail closed; an unknown consumer is not a safe consumer.**

**★★★ THE ROLE-BASED POLICY — minted, and its default is the load-bearing part.** Not every unbindable item must block: **mandatory entry / session / direction / invalidation rule → REFUSE the backtest** · **optional commentary or non-executable annotation → may remain unresolved, but MUST be visibly reported** · ★★★ **UNKNOWN ROLE → REFUSE BY DEFAULT.** That last arm is the one that matters and it matches this campaign's standing law that an **absent constraint means MAXIMUM scope and must fail CLOSED**. ★★ **For `overnight` specifically, refusal is MANDATORY: [MEASURED, R-418] it is a session constraint, and removing it changes WHEN TRADES ARE PERMITTED** — precisely the "run without this rule" conversion the invariant forbids.

**EVIDENCE INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED.** ★★ **[MEASURED HERE, TREE `runtime-production`]** the refusal payload the review specifies is buildable from data already in hand at the binding site: `condition_id`, `type`, `role`, `object` (the rule text) and `reason` are all fields of `ConditionBinding`, and the strategy id is the row carrying `compiled_spec`. **A refusal that names strategy + rule text + semantic type + reason costs nothing extra to emit** — I checked before ordering it.

**★★★ CLAIMS VERIFIED — THE CATCH, CHECKED AT THE LINE.** The critique argues detection-conservatism does not imply execution-conservatism, via fill/consumption semantics. **[MEASURED HERE] it is right, and here is the arithmetic:** `fvg_native.py:126` fills a zone at the first later bar where `low[j] <= z.upper and high[j] >= z.lower` — **an overlap test, which a WIDER band satisfies at an earlier-or-equal bar (bigger `upper` and smaller `lower` each make both comparisons easier).** `:146` then keeps a zone active only until `filled_at_idx`, and `compute_fvg_signal` returns exactly those `bullish_active` / `bearish_active` arrays as its output. ★★★ **Therefore, for any zone BOTH definitions create: taught band fills at bar `f_wide`, implemented band at `f_narrow ≥ f_wide`, and on the interval `[f_wide, f_narrow)` THE PRIMITIVE REPORTS A LIVE ZONE THAT THE TEACHER'S RULE HAS ALREADY CONSUMED. That is a signal the teacher did not sanction — the dangerous direction, reached through the fill path rather than the detection path.**

**★★ SO THE HONEST TWO-LAYER VERDICT, replacing R-410's single one.** **Detection layer: the primitive creates a SUBSET of taught zones** (`low[i] > high[i-2]` is strictly harder than `open[i] > close[i-2]` — R-411's arithmetic, unchanged and still correct). **Signal layer: for each shared zone the primitive is a SUPERSET in DURATION.** ★★★ **Neither set contains the other. For 0159's immutable `INSERT ('paper','traderspost',…)` to succeed on replay, at the moment it runs: **(i)** the CHECK permits the pair — that IS (A), which re-opens the hole item 2 closes; **(ii)** something mutates the tuple before the CHECK evaluates — a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger; **(iii)** the constraint is absent — contradicts 0208. ★ **I went looking for a fourth branch and could not find one: a CHECK is not DEFERRABLE in Postgres, so deferral is out; a trigger returning NULL to skip the row is a variant of (ii) and is silent in the same way; deleting or re-seeding rows in a later migration does not change what 0159 itself inserts on replay. The enumeration holds.**

**EVIDENCE INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED.** ★★ **The cited precedent is real and I verified it at the file rather than from memory:** `0058_audit_log_append_only.sql` — `RETURNS TRIGGER … RAISE EXCEPTION 'audit_log is append-only' … BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE`. **It REJECTS.** And I widened the check past the one instance to the class: a schema-wide grep for `NEW.<col> :=` returns **nothing** — **there is no rewriting-trigger precedent in this codebase at all. Rejection is the house pattern, and (C) would have introduced the first silent-rewrite trigger on the broker table.** ★ Its argument stands on its own merits too: **a genuine future mis-seed of `paper→traderspost` would be recorded as a SUCCESS with different data than was asked for — an unenforced label answered by an invisible correction, which is `'paper'`-is-a-mode one layer deeper.**

**TESTS RERUN (command + result).** `git show ccce6bdf --stat` → **one file, test-only, +40/−4; no SQL touched, 0208 unchanged, 0159 untouched.** Register contents as shipped confirm the two-class split with 0159's reasoning, the fresh-bootstrap-unaffected proof, and the journal-keyed-runner note inline. **CI at ruling time: 2 pass, 13 pending, 0 fail** — the `newFailures: []` expectation is NOT yet observed and I am not treating pending as green.

**ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS TOUCHED.** None in SQL. ★★★ **The one that decided this ruling: "never take a real risk to remove an appearance." (C) would have bought a green replay test — an APPEARANCE of full idempotency — by installing a mechanism that silently alters money-path writes. (B) buys nothing cosmetic and states the truth: 0159 is not replayable, here is exactly why, here is who is unaffected.** ★ **A register entry that says "this cannot re-apply, by design, because X" is stronger engineering than a trigger that makes the failure disappear.**

**FAILED OR UNPROVEN CONDITIONS.** ★★ **The worker's own honest limit, which I am promoting rather than softening: (B) makes a TRUE STATEMENT about the world; it does not make 0159 replayable. **REQUIRED CORRECTIONS.** None. ★ **One thing I want on the record as exemplary rather than corrected: the register's CAPTION was rewritten, not just its list.** It previously described exactly one class while about to hold two — **a false caption that would have taught the next reader something untrue about all nine pre-existing entries.** Fixing the label alongside the data is caption-is-a-claim applied without being told.

**STOP CONDITION.** Any pass-2 failure outside the eleven → revert, do not extend the register.

**LESSON TO PERSIST.** ★★★ **THE DESK'S PRIOR WAS THE WEAKEST EVIDENCE IN THE ROOM AND IT WAS MINE. **§1 — THE CAUSE, [MEASURED HERE] BY EXECUTION.** The A-11 file mocks `pipeline-control-service` as `isActive: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(true)` — a **bare boolean**. `checkProbeGate()` does `if (!(await isPipelineActive().catch(() => false)))`. I ran it in node: `mockIsActive().catch(...)` → **`TypeError: mockIsActive(...).catch is not a function`**, thrown SYNCHRONOUSLY; the same expression against a real `async` function resolves fine. **That TypeError escapes `checkProbeGate()` and lands in `probeTradersPostApiKeys()`'s outer fail-soft `try/catch`, which logs a warn and returns — so the probe never reaches `fetch`, never queries accounts, never notifies.** ★ **The real module is `export async function isActive()`, so this is a TEST-HARNESS defect and NOT a production defect.** The mock was adequate for every pre-R-359 caller (`await` unwraps a plain value happily); R-359's gate introduced the first `.catch()` chaining, and the mock has been quietly incompatible since that moment.

**§2 — A REFUTED HYPOTHESIS OF MINE, RECORDED BECAUSE THE NEAR-MISS IS INSTRUCTIVE.** I first concluded the mock exported the WRONG SYMBOL (`isActive` vs the gate's `isPipelineActive`) — a clean, plausible story. **`broker-router.ts:29` refutes it: `import { isActive as isPipelineActive }`. The mock exports exactly the right name; the alias is local.** Had I published on the strength of the two names differing, I would have sent you to rename a correct mock. **The import line is one line away from the call site, and reading it was the whole difference between a diagnosis and a wild goose chase.**

**§3 — ★★★ AND NOW THE PART THAT UNBLOCKS YOU: YOUR MUTATION EXPERIMENT WAS NEVER NEEDED, BECAUSE THE ARMED RUN ALREADY CONTAINS THE PROOF. What did we want from R-370 §4? WE HAVE EXACTLY THAT CONDITION, ACCIDENTALLY AND AT FULL STRENGTH: the probe is dead in that suite (§1), and under that identical condition the four rewritten tests are RED — while THIS MORNING, under the same dead-probe condition, their pre-rewrite versions were GREEN (that is precisely the vacuity we measured). SAME CONDITION, OLD ASSERTIONS PASS, NEW ASSERTIONS FAIL. That is a before/after on the real runner, and it is a stronger demonstration than the scratch mutation would have given.** ★★ **R-370 §4's acceptance is MET. I am not asking you to re-run it.** This is the skill's standing instruction earning its keep: *ask what is ENTAILED by results already in hand before ordering new work* — the evidence was collected for one purpose and settles another.

**§4 — ★★ A REAL, SMALL PRODUCTION FINDING THE SAME LINE EXPOSES. `checkProbeGate()` declares in its own docstring that "every error path returns a skip reason (fail-CLOSED)". The kill-switch clause honours that with `try/catch → "kill_switch_error"`. THE PIPELINE CLAUSE DOES NOT: `.catch()` chaining catches a REJECTED PROMISE but not a SYNCHRONOUS THROW, so a sync failure there escapes the gate entirely and is swallowed upstream as a generic probe failure — with no skip reason, no telemetry, and no distinction from "the probe ran and found nothing."** Low severity (the real `isActive` is async and unlikely to throw synchronously), but it is the gate's own stated contract, violated on one of four clauses. **ORDERED: bring the pipeline clause to the same `try/catch → "pipeline_error"` shape as the kill-switch clause.** ★ **Note what the two together demonstrate: DEFENSIVE FAIL-SOFT AROUND A WHOLE FUNCTION CONVERTS ITS IMPLEMENTATION ERRORS INTO SILENCE. The outer catch that makes the probe non-blocking is exactly what hid a TypeError meaning "this code is broken" for the entire life of this thread.**

**§5 — AUTHORIZED NOW, TO THIS SEAT.** (a) `isActive: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true)` in the A-11 mock (and audit that file's other mocks for the same promise/value mismatch against how the code now calls them). ## R-358 · 2026-07-28 · AR-327 ruled (short) — **APPROVE** the correction; ★★★ the root cause is better than the correction: **A REPORT HAS ONE TENSE BUT MANY VINTAGES**, and a repair between two measurements silently splits them

**RULING ID:** R-358 · **TASK ID:** AR-326 stat discrepancy · **DECISION:** **APPROVE** — cause identified, immaterial to substance, and the lesson is a genuine addition.

**CLAIMS VERIFIED:** already measured at this desk in R-357 — `git diff --stat` → **18 insertions / 3 deletions**, taken POST-fix, which is precisely why it disagreed. **TESTS RERUN:** none needed; the disputed value was itself my independent measurement. **EVIDENCE INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED:** the diff hunks (248-261, 369-391, nothing at `:58`) stand as ruled.

**ROOT CAUSE ACCEPTED AS DIAGNOSED, and it is this campaign's founding law turned on its author: the `19/4` came from the command batch that also reported `16 failed` — the run taken WHILE `:58` was still mutated. The line-by-line audit was re-taken after the repair and was correct; the STAT was not re-taken and was carried across it. VERIFY THE TREE YOU SHIP, NOT THE ONE YOU BUILT — the law AR-320 §0 opened this entire thread with, broken two reports later on its author's own artifact.**

★★★ **MINTED, generalising the worker's §2 further than it went: A REPORT HAS ONE TENSE BUT MANY VINTAGES. Prose reads as a single "now," but the numbers inside it were measured at different moments, and nothing in the writing carries a timestamp — so a repair occurring between two measurements silently splits a report into fresh claims and stale ones that look identical.** ★★ **And the worker's own framing deserves the sharper statement: it ran the STRONG instrument (line-by-line) post-fix and quoted the WEAK one (stat) pre-fix — so INSTRUMENT STRENGTH AND INSTRUMENT VINTAGE ARE INDEPENDENT PROPERTIES, and a process that tracks only strength will publish a fresh-looking stale number every time. This is the same shape as R-352's `npm install` finding (source verified, environment unverified) and R-348 §2's two-tree error (code from one checkout, config from another): three instances now of MIXED-PROVENANCE EVIDENCE PRESENTED AS ONE MEASUREMENT.**

**REQUIRED CORRECTIONS:** standing form, cheap and mechanical — **after any repair, RE-TAKE every measurement the report will quote, not merely the one that failed.** A number that survived a repair without being re-measured is stale by default, and the cost of re-taking a `--numstat` is nothing against the cost of a stale figure in the record. **SCOPE:** none — no work outstanding. **ACCEPTANCE:** already met. **STOP CONDITION:** n/a. **LESSON TO PERSIST:** the two mints above; and the meta-point that this was caught by re-executing rather than reading, which is now the fourth catch in this thread from the same method.

## R-356 · 2026-07-28 · AR-325 ruled — **APPROVE the discrimination; MY R-355 MONEY-PATH PREMISE IS WITHDRAWN**; ★★★ and the measurement goes one step past H3: **the hardening changed the INNOVATION-DISTRIBUTION PREMISE, not just the number — the stale test's process is mathematically incapable of clearing the new bar (ceiling ≈0.77 vs required 3.0; Student-t(5) scores 23.4)**

**RULING ID:** R-356 · **TASK ID:** R-355 H1/H2 discrimination · **DECISION:** **APPROVE** (discrimination correct, verified here) with one required correction to my own escalation and a fix now specified by measurement rather than by preference.

**CLAIMS VERIFIED — by reading the executable lines at this desk, not by accepting the report:** (1) `synthetic_market_simulator.py:219` is `kurt = float(np.mean(((rets - np.mean(rets)) / std) ** 4) - 3.0)` — **the `-3.0` is a hand-rolled EXCESS correction, so my H1 (Fisher/Pearson convention mismatch) is refuted by arithmetic, exactly as reported;** (2) `:126` shows the old `_MIN_KURTOSIS = 0.3`, `:136` the new `3.0`, and `:133` the hardening note that predicted this breakage in writing; (3) the failing test builds its own GARCH inline (`omega, alpha, beta = 0.00001, 0.10, 0.85`, `eps = rng.standard_normal()`) and **never calls the simulator's generator** — so the 0.461 is a property of the test's toy process.

**EVIDENCE INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED / TESTS RERUN:** R-355's suites (21 passed parity; 149 passed / 1 failed forensics slice), plus a computation at this desk on the test's exact parameters: **theoretical excess kurtosis for GARCH(1,1) with GAUSSIAN innovations = 6α²/(1−3α²−2αβ−β²) = 0.7742** (finite, since 0.9225 < 1); **sampled at n = 200,000 → 0.7136**, converging to theory; **the same process with Student-t(5) innovations → 23.43.**

★★★ **WHAT THAT MEASUREMENT ADDS BEYOND H3, AND IT IS THE ACTIONABLE PART: the failing test cannot reach 3.0 — not "unreliably," but with a mathematical ceiling near 0.77, roughly a quarter of the bar. No seed and no sample size fixes it. And line `:130` states the reason in the constant's own justification — `SF_MIN_EXCESS_KURTOSIS — Student-t innovations guarantee this`. SO THE 0.3 → 3.0 HARDENING WAS NOT A TIGHTENING OF A NUMBER, IT WAS A CHANGE OF THE ASSUMED INNOVATION DISTRIBUTION, and the stale test was written for the old regime. That reframes the fix: it is not "tune a threshold," it is "the test must exercise the regime the threshold now assumes."**

**ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS TOUCHED — AND MY OWN ESCALATION PREMISE IS WITHDRAWN, PLAINLY: R-355 argued that if the simulator under-produces fat tails then every drawdown / ruin / prop-firm-breach probability derived from it is biased optimistic. THE FAILURE CARRIES ZERO INFORMATION ABOUT THE SIMULATOR — the number never passed through it. The reasoning was sound and the premise was false, and a sound argument on a false premise is still wrong.** The worker's honest bound is adopted verbatim: **refuting my premise is NOT the same as clearing the simulator — whether the simulator's OWN generator clears 3.0 is a separate question this test does not ask, and it remains UNMEASURED.**

**REQUIRED CORRECTIONS:** (1) **Fix the test by giving its generator Student-t innovations**, matching the premise the constant's own comment states — then it exercises the regime the bar was hardened for, and (measured above) clears it by ~8×. **Do NOT instead lower the threshold or pass a small explicit `min_kurtosis`: that leaves a green test asserting a bar production does not use.** Note the sibling at `:236` already passes `min_kurtosis=1.0` explicitly, so the parameter is overridable and the pattern exists — which is precisely why the stale test's reliance on the default went unnoticed. (2) **Answer the open question separately: does the simulator's own generator clear 3.0?** That is the question my escalation should have asked, and it is still worth asking. (3) Keep `:233`'s white-noise negative case passing — the corrected check must still reject a Gaussian series.

**FILES/SCOPE ALLOWED:** `src/engine/tests/test_synthetic_market_simulator.py` only for (1); read-only for (2). **Forbidden:** changing `_MIN_KURTOSIS`, changing `:219`'s statistic, or touching the simulator to make a test pass. **ACCEPTANCE COMMANDS:** `python -m pytest src/engine/tests/test_synthetic_market_simulator.py -q` fully green, **plus a red-proof that reverting the innovations to Gaussian returns the failure** — the fix must be shown to be the thing that fixed it. **STOP CONDITION:** stop and report if (2) finds the simulator's own generator below 3.0 — that is the money-path question my premise wrongly claimed was already answered.

★★ **LESSON TO PERSIST — two, and the first is mine: AN INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY SIGNAL IS A HYPOTHESIS GENERATOR, NOT EVIDENCE. My "the sibling test's bar is 1.0, so 3.0 is out of family" was a reasonable tell and it pointed at the wrong file's looser assertion; the arithmetic settled in one line what the pattern-matching could not. And the worker's: A HARDENING THAT PREDICTS WHICH TESTS IT WILL BREAK, AND DOES NOT FIX THEM, CONVERTS A DELIBERATE IMPROVEMENT INTO PERMANENT RED — which on a branch with no CI (R-350 §2) is indistinguishable from never having looked. ## R-355 · 2026-07-28 · ★★★ FIRST RULING IN THE STRUCTURED FORM — and it exists because I ran tests instead of reading about them, which found **A DETERMINISTIC FAILING TEST NO REPORT HAS EVER MENTIONED**

Assertion: `fail_reasons: ['kurtosis_0.461_below_3.0']`. The file's own sibling tests treat `stats["kurtosis"]` as **EXCESS** kurtosis (`:212` "Excess kurtosis must be > 0 (fat tails vs Gaussian)"; `:234` "white noise (kurtosis ~= 0)"; `:220` asserts `> 1.0` as the *high* bar for a t(4) distribution). **The failing calibration compares that same excess measurement against 3.0.**

**TESTS RERUN:** `pytest src/engine/tests/test_session_windows_parity.py src/engine/tests/test_session_windows.py` → 21 passed. `pytest src/engine/tests/ -k "calibration or fidelity or tooth"` → 149 passed, 3 skipped, **1 failed**, 8195 deselected, 40.6s.

**ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS TOUCHED:** synthetic-market realism feeds risk estimation. **If the simulator genuinely under-produces fat tails, every drawdown, ruin and prop-firm-breach probability derived from it is biased OPTIMISTIC — tail events are precisely where daily-loss and max-drawdown breaches live.** That is money-path, and it is why this is ESCALATE rather than a note.

**FAILED OR UNPROVEN CONDITIONS — and I am labelling the hypothesis as a hypothesis: (H1, LIKELY, NOT MEASURED) a Fisher/Pearson convention mismatch — 3.0 is the RAW kurtosis of a normal distribution, and comparing it against an EXCESS measurement silently demands raw ≥ 6.0. Excess 0.461 = raw 3.46, which is genuinely fat-tailed and would PASS a raw-scale test. Internal-consistency evidence: the same file's own "high excess kurtosis" bar is 1.0, so a 3.0 excess threshold is out of family with its neighbours. (H2, ALTERNATIVE) the threshold is a deliberate excess-scale bar and the GARCH parameterisation genuinely under-produces tails. THESE HAVE OPPOSITE FIXES — H1 corrects the test, H2 corrects the simulator — and shipping the wrong one either hides a real risk defect or embalms a wrong threshold. NOT MEASURED: which consumers use this simulator on a load-bearing path.**

**REQUIRED CORRECTIONS:** (1) **Discriminate H1 from H2 before touching either side** — read the calibration function's threshold definition for a stated scale (raw vs excess) and check it against a known reference: a normal sample must score ~0 and a t(5) sample ~2 on that statistic; whichever hypothesis survives names the fix. (2) **Enumerate consumers** of the synthetic market simulator — if any Monte Carlo survival, drawdown or prop-firm gate reads it, that gate's outputs inherit the bias and must be re-scoped. (3) Note that this file was last touched by `410b75cf "recovery: restore 86 null-byte-corrupted files"` — **a mass corruption-and-restore event is a legitimate suspect for a silently altered constant**, and the restore should be diffed against its pre-corruption ancestor for this file.

Two individually-defensible defaults combine into a genuinely bad one: R-5's URL constant defaults to the REAL venue when unset, and R-7's probe fires from `setImmediate` AT MODULE LOAD. Put together: AN UNCONFIGURED PROCESS THAT MERELY *IMPORTS* `broker-router.ts` WILL ATTEMPT AN OUTBOUND POST TO PRODUCTION TRADERSPOST. Neither author was careless — a default URL is normal, a boot-time credential check is normal — but the composition is a system that phones the live venue with zero configuration and zero intent.** ★ **`setImmediate` at module scope is the specific error: IMPORT IS NOT INTENT. Any importer fires it — a unit test, a one-off script, a migration runner, a REPL, a type-check that executes the module, a developer's `tsx` session. "On every boot" understates the blast radius; it is "on every import in every process."**

**§2 — ★★★ THE ROOT DEFECT IS ARCHITECTURAL: BROKER EGRESS HAPPENS AT THREE DIFFERENT LEVELS WITH THREE DIFFERENT GATE SETS. R-1/R-2 pass `checkRoutingGuard()` then `routeOrder()`'s stack. R-3 enters `routeOrder()` DIRECTLY, skipping `checkRoutingGuard()` entirely — which is why the execution-mode flag does not govern it. R-7 bypasses both and calls `fetch` itself. THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING RESTATED AS A CAUSE: the gates are attached to CALLERS, so every new caller is a new opportunity to miss one, and the enumeration we just ran is a thing we will have to run again after every feature.** ★★ **THE FIX I WOULD SHIP, and it is one unit rather than five: (1) ONE egress function — the only place in the codebase permitted to perform an HTTP request to a broker host — with the full stack INSIDE it (kill switch, pipeline pause, execution-mode flag, lifecycle, account-enabled, credential load); (2) every existing path re-pointed through it, including the probe; (3) A TEST THAT FAILS IF ANY OTHER MODULE CALLS `fetch`/`axios`/`http.request` WITH A BROKER HOST — the same AST-shaped sweep AR-320 just performed by hand, turned into a guard that runs in CI. ★ That converts "six gates to keep correct forever" into "one chokepoint plus a test that nothing bypasses it," and it closes the class at its defining property — outbound egress to a broker — rather than at the five instances we happen to have found.** Red-proof at birth: add a `fetch` to a broker host in a scratch module and the test must go RED.

**§3 — R-3(b) IS NOT MERELY A GATE GAP, IT IS AN AUTHORIZATION CONFUSION. The caller authenticates as an ASSIGNMENT (its token matches a per-assignment secret), and then SUPPLIES `strategy_id` — a fact the server could derive from the assignment it just authenticated. THE CALLER IS ASSERTING WHAT IT SHOULD BE TOLD.** That is why the `if (strategy_id)` carve-out exists at all, and why "close the carve-out" is the weaker fix: **the correct design makes `strategy_id` server-derived from the authenticated assignment and never read from the request body**, at which point the lifecycle gate is unconditional by construction and cannot be skipped by omission. ★ **THREE MORE THINGS I WANT MEASURED ON THAT ROUTE BEFORE IT IS CALLED SAFE, all standard for a pre-auth internet endpoint and none of them yet checked: (i) IS THE TOKEN COMPARE CONSTANT-TIME? A `===` on a secret is a timing oracle, and this one is reachable without auth. (ii) IS THERE RATE LIMITING? Pre-auth plus no limit is both a brute-force surface against the token and a free DoS. (iii) IS THE TOKEN REPLAYABLE? A static bearer with no nonce or timestamp means one observed request can be replayed forever — and this system DISTRIBUTES Pine scripts to family members, so the token travels inside a file that gets copied. HMAC mode has a signature; static-token mode has nothing.**

**§4 — THE PROBE'S DESIGN, ON ITS OWN TERMS. Validating a credential by SENDING IT TO THE PRODUCTION ENDPOINT means the key lands in the vendor's request logs on every process start — that is not a breach, but it is gratuitous exposure of the most sensitive value in the system, repeated indefinitely. And the "4xx means the key is valid" heuristic is coupled to a third party's error semantics: the day TradersPost returns 200 with an error body, or 401 for a malformed payload, the check silently inverts. ★ THE RIGHT SHAPE: do not probe at boot at all. Validate lazily on first real use, or behind an explicit operator action, with the result cached and a circuit breaker — and if the vendor offers a credential-validation endpoint, use that rather than the order webhook.**

**§5 — ★★ A DEPLOYMENT FINDING THE ENUMERATION IMPLIES AND NOBODY DREW: THE TOWER EXECUTES `hardening/slumhouse-shared-office-parity-20260723` @ `969ba025`, AND THIS REPO'S CI GATES RUN ON WHATEVER BRANCH CI IS CONFIGURED FOR. IF CI GATES `main` WHILE THE TOWER RUNS A HARDENING BRANCH, THEN EVERY GREEN CI RUN IS PROTECTING CODE NOBODY EXECUTES — the guard-aimed-at-the-wrong-subject species, at the deployment layer, where it is most expensive.** ORDERED, and it is two reads: **which branches do the CI workflows trigger on, and did `969ba025` itself ever pass them?** ★ Related and equally cheap: `runtime-production` is a hand-maintained worktree, so **there is no deploy record** — no commit-to-deployment mapping, nothing that says which SHA has been running since when. For a system heading toward live capital, "what is running right now, and who put it there" must be answerable without reading the service registry.

**§6 — PRIORITY, AS AN ENGINEER RATHER THAN AS A PROCESS: do §2 FIRST.** The chokepoint plus its bypass test subsumes R-5 (the default URL lives inside the one egress function and can be made mandatory there), R-7 (the probe routes through the same stack or is deleted), and the ongoing cost of R-1/R-2/R-3 drifting apart. **Then §3's server-derived `strategy_id`, which is a small change with a large contract improvement. Then §5's CI-branch question, because a wrong answer there devalues every green check we have ever cited. The DB read (R-348 §7) stays first in TIME because it costs one query and tells us whether any of this is currently reachable — but it is not the fix, and the fix does not depend on it.** **Holds:** unchanged from R-348 §8.

**§2 — THE MEASURED STATE: worker's last write `AGENT-REPORTS.md` at 05:23:39; last worker commit `a13a4614` at 05:23; checked 06:08 — 45 minutes, both channels silent. HEAD attached (`h1-wave4-sealed12-driver`). No new untracked artifacts; the four `??` files are all pre-existing (dated 07-17 and 07-21).** Cause **(UNTESTED)** — the three candidates remain indistinguishable at this bar: genuine idleness, silent work, or death by external limit (with precedent this session, 00:22–03:26, operator-confirmed). **I am not diagnosing it and I am not nudging on a guess.**

**§3 — ONE THING THE SILENCE IS WEAK EVIDENCE FOR, AND IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN EXCUSE: the ordered task — R-330 §2's `TF_PHASE_5_ENABLED` feasibility read — IS READ-ONLY, so it produces NO commits and NO file writes BY DESIGN. A worker doing exactly what it was told to do is invisible to both channels for the whole duration.** ★ **That is precisely the hole the START-RECEIPT law was minted to close, and this is its cleanest illustration yet: when the ordered work writes nothing, the receipt IS the only signal, and its absence is the only thing that distinguishes working from stopped.** **STATUS-CHECK ISSUED: post a START-RECEIPT or a one-line status for the feasibility read. MINTED: A NARROW PATTERN DOES NOT RETURN NOTHING; IT RETURNS A PLAUSIBLE NUMBER. ## R-327 · 2026-07-28 · AR-310 ruled: **BRANCH α — LATENT, no alarm, nothing to the operator**, on four reads each closing a distinct mechanism; MINT: **A STATE CLAIM IS PROVEN BY CLOSING EACH MECHANISM THAT COULD MAKE IT FALSE**, not by one read plus confidence; ★★ MINT: **A VERIFIED-TRUE CAPTION IS A FINDING TOO** — record confirmations or the record becomes a selection-biased sample; ★★★ MINT: **NAME A GAP BY WHAT IT BLOCKS, NOT BY WHAT IS MISSING** — and the SELF-DECLARED PRECONDITION sweep it implies is ORDERED

**§1 — BRANCH α CONFIRMED, and the method is the reusable part.** Three ways the flag could still have been ON, each closed by a SEPARATE read rather than by reasoning: **a non-default in config** (grep for the flag across every `.env*` under `Projects/` — zero hits, including `runtime-production/.env`, a real 23 KB runtime config rather than a stub); **a second ungated call site** (all references to `evaluateStyleCExit` enumerated — exactly one outside its definition and the parity suite, and it sits inside the flag's own `if`); **a divergent tower checkout** (read directly; identical gate→call shape). ★ And the default is **fail-safe BY CONSTRUCTION, not by configuration**: `=== "true"` strict equality means unset, empty, `"1"` and `"TRUE"` all evaluate false — **there is no value of "absent" that turns it on**, which is a stronger property than any configuration audit could establish. **MINTED as the standing template for every "is X on?" question this campaign will ask before anything goes live: enumerate the mechanisms by which the state could differ from your belief, and close each one by a read.** Per the R-326 §2 pre-registration: **LATENT parity gap, cured by fixtures, no alarm, nothing owed to the operator** — the third pre-registration this arc that bound its author to an outcome they could not negotiate after the fact.

**§2 — ★★ MINTED, and it corrects a bias in our own record: A VERIFIED-TRUE CAPTION IS A FINDING TOO.** The flag's comment — *"SHIPPED OPT-IN / DEFAULT OFF … the default path remains the audited Python handler … Flip only after the evaluator is parity-validated"* — **matches the behaviour exactly**, and the worker was right to state that explicitly rather than pass over it. **This campaign has spent two days publishing captions that were false and has published almost none that were true, which makes our own record a selection-biased sample: we know the numerator far better than the denominator, and a reader of the ledger alone would conclude this codebase lies more than it does.** Record the confirmations alongside the convictions — it costs a sentence, it prices the real defect rate honestly, and it identifies the surfaces whose captions can be trusted.

**§3 — ★★★ THE REFRAMING IS THE BEST THING IN THE REPORT AND I AM ELEVATING IT TO A STANDING RULE: NAME A GAP BY WHAT IT BLOCKS, NOT BY WHAT IS MISSING.** "The chandelier fallback lacks cross-runtime parity coverage" is open-ended hardening with no finish line; **"the flag's own stated precondition for flipping it is NOT met, and the chandelier fixtures are what would meet it"** is a gated deliverable that is done when it is done. **§4 — ★ THE SELF-CORRECTION IS CREDITED AT FULL WEIGHT BECAUSE THE ANSWER WAS RIGHT.** The earlier statement that the flag was off rested on the code default, not on a read of the tower's config — *"the statement survives the measurement, but it was a claim ahead of its evidence at the moment I made it."* **A claim ahead of its evidence is a process defect even when it turns out true, because the process is what generalises and the answer is not.** And the judgement that no operator follow-up was owed — same answer, now measured — is correct: a correction notice for a statement that survived its own measurement would be noise, and this desk's discipline is to correct what is WRONG, not to perform correction.

## R-324 · 2026-07-28 · AR-307 ruled: the collapse is ACCEPTED — **every floor on a collection is UNBOUNDED DOWNWARD BY CONSTRUCTION, so slack is FUSE LENGTH, not the presence of the defect**, and all 69 are in the class; ★ **I ORDERED A RE-SORT TWICE AND BOTH TIMES PRESUMED THE CLASS WAS HETEROGENEOUS** — MINT: a criterion that returns the same answer for every member is a MEMBERSHIP TEST, not a sort key; ★★ REFINEMENT: unbounded-downward is a defect UNLESS it is the requirement — **the discriminator is whether the number is a SPECIFICATION or an ARTIFACT of the population at writing time**; the 194 `>0` assertions are resolved onto the SAME axis without sweeping them in

**§1 — THE COLLAPSE IS RIGHT AND I ACCEPT IT AGAINST MY OWN TWO ORDERS.** A floor `>= N` on a collection of size M permits losing (M−N) members today and permits losing one the instant the population reaches N+1 — **so the property that makes it dangerous is not today's gap but that it is unbounded downward by construction; the Style C gate proves it, with zero slack, biting today, and one added fixture away from licensing a deletion.** ★ **My share is precise: R-322 §4 ordered the zero-slack floors "re-examined" and R-323 §5 ordered the population "sorted by would-this-still-be-correct-if-it-grew-by-one" — and that criterion answers NO FOR EVERY MEMBER. MINTED: A CRITERION THAT RETURNS THE SAME ANSWER FOR EVERY MEMBER IS A MEMBERSHIP TEST, NOT A SORT KEY — and A RE-SORT PRESUMES THE CLASS IS HETEROGENEOUS, so verify that before ordering one.** I corrected the criterion twice while keeping the wrong frame: I kept assuming some floors were safe. The worker's own diagnosis is the general form and it is the habit both desks keep repeating — **ranking by an OBSERVABLE that correlated with the defect in the members you happened to examine is sampling the correlation, not the property.**

**§2 — ★★ ONE REFINEMENT THAT SHARPENS THE BOUNDARY AND MAKES CURE-SELECTION MECHANICAL. "Unbounded downward" is a defect UNLESS unbounded-downward is the actual requirement — a quorum gate asserting `>= 3 sources` is not an armed fuse, it is a SPECIFICATION, and losing members down to three is permitted by design. THE DISCRIMINATOR: IS THE NUMBER A SPECIFICATION, OR AN ARTIFACT OF THE POPULATION'S SIZE WHEN THE LINE WAS WRITTEN? `>= 3` for quorum is a specification; `>= 14` against exactly 14, and `>= 50` against 108, are artifacts — snapshots rounded down.** The question is answerable per site in one sentence — *where did this number come from?* — and it selects the cure directly: **an ARTIFACT number is replaced by a membership assertion; a SPECIFICATION number keeps its floor and gets its justification made assertable (R-316 §4).** That also gives the class its honest name: not "every floor is a defect," but **every floor is unbounded downward, and that is a defect wherever the bound was a snapshot rather than a requirement.**

**§3 — THE ORDERING IS RECONCILED RATHER THAN WITHDRAWN: MEMBERSHIP IN THE CLASS IS UNIFORM; THE PRIORITY OF CURE IS NOT.** Sorting by slack was wrong because slack does not determine defecthood — but the 67 remaining still need an order of work, and **consequence-of-silent-loss genuinely varies**: a lost rail, gate, risk parameter or registry entry costs more than a lost cosmetic collection, which is why the scheduler pair earned its place first. **ORDERED: work the 67 in order of what a silently-lost member costs, with the defect's presence taken as given for all of them.**

**§4 — THE 194 `> 0` ASSERTIONS: RESOLVED ONTO THE EXISTING AXIS, NEITHER SWEPT IN NOR LEFT OPEN.** The restraint that refused to fold them in by analogy is exactly right — *"sweeping 194 sites in on an argument-by-analogy is how a class census over-reaches"* — and it is also right that they are not simply out. **They are not a separate question: they are 194 instances of the SAME question that separated the 69 from the 19 — does this collection have MEMBERS whose silent loss matters, or is EXISTENCE the whole claim?** A `>0` over a registry, a rail set or a fixture set is the same defect wearing a smaller number; a `>0` over "the parse returned something" or "the query returned rows" is correct as written, because non-emptiness IS the specification (and by §2, that number is a specification, not an artifact). **ORDERED as a CLASSIFICATION, not as 194 fixes: sort the 194 by whether the collection's membership is load-bearing; only the load-bearing subset inherits the 69's treatment.** Cheap, and it closes the question without over-reaching in either direction. **§5 — The three cures are RATIFIED with §2's selection rule attached: enumerated set with meaningful members → a GENERATED required-NAME assertion; set with a computable counterpart → the two-artifact comparison (scheduler form), preferring a shared ORACLE where one can be authored (R-322 §3); genuinely open-ended with a specification bound → keep the floor and make the excuse assertable. Per-site sizing is ENDORSED over budgeting 69 mechanical edits, and the 19 string-length exclusions stand on a real property distinction — a string has no membership to lose.**

**§6 — Honest state accepted:** 67 of 69 untouched, true populations behind them not re-measured, and the distinction that does not decide membership is correctly not presented as if it did. **Sequence:** finish the 13/13 Style C derivation (R-323 §3) → exit-path branch coverage (R-323 §4) → the 67 floors in consequence order under §2's cure-selection rule → the 194 `>0` classification (§4) → manifest cures (R-320 §2) → make-the-excuse-assertable unit (R-319 §5) → (a)/(c) re-measure (R-322 §6) → aid families 7 and 8 → R-317 follow-ons → noisy-guard sweep → mirror-the-logic sweep → artifact-staleness CLASS census → disposition unit by species → 3-ii (+(b) migration) → 3-iii → R-304 §3 code guard → builds. **Holds:** flags OFF · FRAME HOLDS (strict floor 1) · **floor class corrected to 69 uniform members with a specification-vs-artifact discriminator** · corpus = 16 · 0 eligible today (honest) · the 77 sealed-and-durable · nothing live.

## R-323 · 2026-07-28 · AR-306 ruled: §4 CLOSED with a two-way red-proof and a hash-verified restore; ★★★ THE SHAPE RESULT IS THE PRIZE — **WHEN A POPULATION MAY GROW BUT MUST NOT SHRINK, THE INVARIANT IS OVER MEMBERSHIP, NOT CARDINALITY**, and NO count-shaped assertion can satisfy both directions — **so my own "tighten to equality" target form was wrong**; ★★★ provenance ruled SPEC-CONSISTENT-NOT-INDEPENDENT, MINT: **EVIDENCE CONSISTENT WITH BOTH HYPOTHESES IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR EITHER**; ★★ **I CORRECT MY R-322 §3** — capture does not degrade the oracle to "B matches A", it EMBALMS a capture-time bug — and the cure is **PROVENANCE IS ARCHAEOLOGY; DERIVABILITY IS MEASUREMENT**

MINTED: WHEN A POPULATION MAY GROW BUT MUST NOT SHRINK, THE INVARIANT IS OVER MEMBERSHIP, NOT CARDINALITY — cardinality conflates growth with loss; membership distinguishes them, and it names the lost scenario instead of printing a number.** ★ **THAT CONVICTS MY OWN TARGET FORM: R-311 §4 and R-316 §3 ordered floors "tightened to equality," and equality is WRONG for any population that may legitimately grow. Fifth instance of the same habit — I specified the mechanism (equality) where the property was strict-downward-and-permissive-upward. THE TARGET FORM FOR THE WHOLE FLOOR POPULATION IS CORRECTED: a GENERATED required-membership assertion plus uniqueness, not an equality and not a floor.**

**§2 — ★ ONE OPERATIONAL LAW, EARNED THE HARD WAY AND ALMOST NEEDED: the first red-proof run CRASHED mid-harness on a subprocess decoding error, and the `finally` had already restored the production artifact byte-exact before the traceback printed. A MUTATION HARNESS OVER A REAL ARTIFACT NEEDS ITS RESTORE TO SURVIVE THE HARNESS'S OWN FAILURE, NOT ONLY ITS SUCCESS** — restore in a `finally`, and verify the restoration BY HASH rather than assuming it. Banked as standing form for every in-place mutation proof this campaign runs.

**§3 — ★★★ PROVENANCE: RULED SPEC-CONSISTENT, NOT INDEPENDENT — and the reasoning is the finest thing in the report.** History bounds it partly (`style_c_handler.py` 2026-05-19, the TS evaluator and the fixture both 2026-06-29, so capture from TS is impossible), and 11 of 13 expected decisions re-derive by hand from the fixture's own stated arithmetic with NEITHER engine imported. **But a capture from a CORRECT engine yields values that are equally derivable — so 11/13 is consistent with both hypotheses and discriminates neither. That was imprecise and understated it in one direction while overstating it in another: A FROZEN FIXTURE, HOWEVER IT WAS AUTHORED, STILL CATCHES ALL FUTURE DRIFT INCLUDING CO-DRIFT — because it does not move when the engines do. What capture actually does is EMBALM ANY BUG PRESENT IN THE SOURCE ENGINE AT CAPTURE TIME, and then guard BOTH engines into reproducing it. That is the assert-embalms-a-dead-value species at fixture scale, and it is a different risk than the one I named: not co-drift, but a possible 2026-05-19-era Python behaviour frozen into the oracle.** ★★★ **THE CONSTRUCTIVE ORDER, because provenance may be unknowable and does not need to be known: PROVENANCE IS ARCHAEOLOGY; DERIVABILITY IS MEASUREMENT. ## R-322 · 2026-07-28 · AR-305 ruled: the sample's METHOD is accepted and its NUMBER is WITHDRAWN — ★★★ MINT: **THE DIRECTION OF AN INSTRUMENT'S ERROR IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A DEDUCTION** (the script called itself an upper bound; both hand-checks moved the other way); ★★★ **THE MONEY-PATH HEAD IS ALREADY ENFORCED** — severity-first ordering did its job by putting the biggest nomination under verification first; ★★★ a FIFTH cure is named — **ORACLE-ENFORCED, which is STRICTLY STRONGER than direct comparison because A-vs-B passes when both drift together**; the delay-fused floor is RULED TOUCHABLE

**§1 — Sample method ACCEPTED (seed 20260728, n=25, all paths published); its RATE WITHDRAWN, and the withdrawal is the finding.** Two of the 21 MENTION verdicts were hand-checked and **both were false negatives** — `session_windows` nominated against the GENERATOR rather than the exhaustive parity test it built yesterday, and `style-c-exit-evaluator.ts` scored MENTION against a file **literally named `…-parity.test.ts`**. ★ **The script declared itself "an upper bound — the proxy is deliberately generous." It is not generous; it UNDER-counts. MINTED: THE DIRECTION OF AN INSTRUMENT'S ERROR IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A DEDUCTION — a bound asserted by reasoning about the instrument's design is not a bound, and mislabelling the direction is worse than publishing a bare number, because a bound LICENSES downstream reasoning ("at most 16% enforced, so at least 84% is work") that a bare number does not.** The test is cheap and was available all along: hand-check a handful and see which way they move; here 2 of 2 moved against the claimed direction. **This is the third time this campaign has reasoned about an instrument instead of testing it** — the prove-the-arms-are-distinct probe, the RAW/NORM classifier, and now an error-bar's sign — so the standing form is: **an instrument's own properties are as much subject to measurement as its outputs.**

**§2 — ★★★ THE MONEY-PATH HEAD IS ENFORCED, MEASURED: `style-c-exit-evaluator-parity.test.ts` loads `tests/fixtures/style_c_parity_fixtures.json` — the SAME file the Python twin runs through `style_c_handler.py` — and asserts identical `decision` and `new_stop`.** I ranked that pairing the head of the drift-hazard bucket because a Python↔TS disagreement on the EXIT path is a wrong exit and a wrong exit is money; the ranking rested on a NOMINATION, and the nomination is disconfirmed. ★ **That is the ordering working, not failing: SEVERITY-FIRST ORDERING IS A VERIFICATION ORDER, NOT A WORK ORDER — its purpose is to put the highest-consequence claim under a check first, and the cheapest possible outcome is exactly this, the head disconfirmed in one step before any work was built on it.** Good news, measured.

**§3 — ★★★ A FIFTH CURE, AND IT OUTRANKS THE ONE I MADE THE REFERENCE. The shared-fixture pattern — neither engine compared to the other, both compared to ONE ORACLE — is a legitimate enforcement class my taxonomy had no name for. And it is not merely equal to direct comparison, it is STRICTLY STRONGER: A DIRECT A-vs-B COMPARISON PASSES WHEN BOTH SIDES DRIFT TOGETHER; A COMPARISON AGAINST A SHARED ORACLE DOES NOT. Prefer an oracle wherever one can be authored.** ★ **This also NAMES what R-317 §4 ordered: publishing the 18 boundary minutes in CLAUDE.md converts `killzone.ts`-as-authority into an ORACLE both implementations are checked against — the same pattern, arrived at independently, which is the best evidence the pattern is right.** ★★ **QUALIFICATION, from the registry's own caution and it is load-bearing: AN ORACLE IS ONLY AS INDEPENDENT AS ITS EXPECTED VALUES' DERIVATION. If a fixture's expected values were CAPTURED FROM ONE ENGINE, that engine cannot fail and the "oracle" degrades to "B matches A" wearing a stronger name. ORDERED: determine how `style_c_parity_fixtures.json`'s expected `decision`/`new_stop` were derived — authored from the spec, or recorded from an engine — and label the entry accordingly.** ★ And my taxonomy is now incomplete for the SECOND time on the same population — first no residual, now a missing legitimate cure — so it stands corrected as **(a) direct-comparison-enforced · (b) construction-enforced · (c) manual-unenforced · (d) no referent · (e) ORACLE-ENFORCED**, with (e) ranked above (a).

**§4 — THE DELAY-FUSED FLOOR: RULED — TOUCH IT.** `expect(fixtures.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(14)` against a true count of exactly 14 has zero slack today and genuinely bites, **but its correctness is a coincidence of the population's current size: add a fifteenth fixture and it silently licenses dropping back to fourteen, with nobody having edited the guard.** ★ **MINTED: A GUARD WHOSE CORRECTNESS DEPENDS ON THE POPULATION NOT CHANGING IS CORRECT BY COINCIDENCE — an equality is self-maintaining; a floor is a non-biter with a delay fuse, and it is INVISIBLE AT BIRTH because the confessional comment ("14 at time of writing") would have been RIGHT.** Fifth way a guard stops guarding untouched. The change is one line — `=== fixtures.length` derived by computation — and it is ordered WITH its red-proof: removing a fixture must go RED, and adding one must stay GREEN with no edit to the guard. ★★ **AND THE CONSEQUENCE FOR WORK ALREADY DONE: R-316 §5's 168 floors were dispositioned by SLACK, so every zero-slack floor would have been classified harmless. ORDERED: re-examine that sub-population — zero-slack floors are the delay-fused set, not the safe set.**

**§5 — The KNOWN-ANSWER REGISTRY is ACCEPTED, and its CAUTION section is the load-bearing half.** Six entries each carrying its value, HOW it was established, and its date — and, decisively, what it did NOT settle: entry 1 records that two implementations AGREE, not that the 18 minutes are right against any external ICT source; entry 6 records that both engines run the same fixtures, not that the fixtures were derived independently of either. **A control used past its scope is an unverified premise wearing a measurement's authority, and a registry that recorded conclusions rather than scopes would manufacture exactly that.** "Records what each measurement SETTLED, not what it suggests" is the standard. **§6 — THE WITHDRAWAL WITHOUT SUBSTITUTION IS CREDITED AND ITS PROPAGATION RULED: refusing to publish a corrected rate because "two spot-checks do not make an estimate" is R-315's correction-inherits-its-error applied by the desk that was taught it. HONEST STATE, both buckets: (a)=209 is UNMEASURED with a demonstrated under-counting proxy and two confirmed enforced members; and (c)=144 INHERITS THE SAME BIAS — if the proxy under-counts enforcement, some of the 144 are enforced too, so 144 is an UPPER BOUND ON HAZARDS, not a count. Both published numbers are now known-biased toward OVER-stating the work, which is the better direction to be wrong in and must still be labelled.** The re-measure is ORDERED as a sized unit, specified by PROPERTY not mechanism: **the comparator must determine whether a test EXERCISES both artifacts — or a shared oracle both are bound to — and asserts on the result, rather than merely naming them**; AST analysis, import tracing or execution instrumentation are the implementer's choice, and the full sample gets hand-verification.

## R-321 · 2026-07-28 · AR-304 ruled: the `mirrors` disposition is ACCEPTED **AS NOMINATIONS** (31 / 209 / 144 / **278 with no referent at all**); ★ **MY OWN TAXONOMY WAS INCOMPLETE — 42% of the population fell outside the three classes I ordered** — MINT: EVERY ORDERED TAXONOMY OWES A RESIDUAL CATEGORY; ★★★ MINT: **A DISCLAIMER CAN LAUNDER A DEFECT** — the hedge would have dressed a substring collision as disclosed uncertainty; ★★★ MINT: **THE BEST CONTROL IS A CASE YOU ALREADY ANSWERED BY ANOTHER METHOD**, so a KNOWN-ANSWER REGISTRY is proposed; A SUBSTRING IS NOT A NAMING CONVENTION accepted

**§1 — Disposition ACCEPTED as NOMINATIONS, never as findings: 662 claims — (b) enforced by construction 31 · (a) test-NOMINATED 209 · (c) manual and unenforced 144 · NO REFERENT NAMED 278.** ★ **AND THE FOURTH BUCKET IS MY CORRECTION TO TAKE: R-315 §3 ordered this population sorted into three classes, and 42% of it fits none of them.** A classification ordered without a residual leaves the classifier two options — mis-file the remainder or say nothing — **and both hide the finding**; the worker took neither and added the bucket instead, which is why the largest single fact about this stratum is visible at all. **MINTED: EVERY ORDERED TAXONOMY OWES A RESIDUAL CATEGORY.** This is the fourth time in this arc that a class I specified from imagination proved narrower than the data's own forms — mechanism-not-property, confession-shape, three-instances-as-a-census, and now a taxonomy with no remainder — and they are one habit, not four incidents.

**§2 — ★★★ HOW THE DEFECTS WERE CAUGHT IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART, and the first method deserves a mint. The referent-extraction bug was caught by a CONTROL WHOSE ANSWER WAS ALREADY KNOWN BY INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT — `session_windows`, whose parity test the same desk had built an hour earlier and measured at 40,782 comparisons — and the control printed `INSTRUMENT STILL DEFECTIVE` until it stopped. MINTED: THE BEST CONTROL IS A CASE YOU ALREADY ANSWERED BY ANOTHER METHOD — stronger than a synthetic fixture, because its truth was established by a different instrument and cannot be reproduced by the same bug.** ★ **AND THE COMPOUNDING IS WORTH BUILDING ON: yesterday's measurement became today's control. ORDERED (cheap, additive): keep a KNOWN-ANSWER REGISTRY — cases whose truth was fixed by independent measurement, available as controls for every future instrument.** It already has members: `session_windows` parity 0/40,782 · scheduler 108 · `ALL_STRATS` 174 · the manifest 275/275 · the two de-approximated Population-A kinds. Each new measurement adds one, and every later census gets cheaper and harder to fool.

**§3 — ★★★ THE SHARPEST FINDING IN THE REPORT IS ABOUT REPORTING ITSELF. The worker was about to publish 209 claims as test-backed WITH a hedge — "(a) is weak evidence" — when five of the first six it sampled turned out to be backed by `backtester.py` via a substring collision. Its own sentence: the hedge "would have made it LOOK like disclosed uncertainty rather than an undetected defect." MINTED: A DISCLAIMER CAN LAUNDER A DEFECT. Disclosure does not discharge — this desk has held that for weeks — but this is sharper and worse: a well-placed hedge PRE-ANSWERS the reader's suspicion, so the defect rides through inside the very sentence that looked like candour. ★ THE OPERATIONAL RULE: THE INSTINCT TO HEDGE IS THE SIGNAL TO SAMPLE. When you find yourself about to write "this bucket is weak," stop and measure HOW weak — the impulse to qualify is evidence you already doubt the number, and doubt is cheap to convert into a count.** Credit where it belongs: what triggered the sampling was the worker applying R-312's own twin mint to itself — a characterisation that sets a conclusion owes the same verification as a number that sets a gate.

"A test names both sides" ≠ "a test asserts they agree," and the sample is what converts 209 from unknown to bounded. (c) 144 — SEVERITY-ORDERED BY MONEY-PATH PROXIMITY, and the report already names the head: `style-c-exit-evaluator.ts` claiming to mirror `price_reached()` in `style_c_handler.py` is a Python↔TS parity claim ON THE EXIT PATH, where a disagreement is a wrong exit and a wrong exit is money; `paper-signal-service.ts` (4) next; then the rest of the 120 files. (278) NO REFERENT — the cure is a writing rule, not an investigation: A MIRRORS-CLAIM MUST NAME ITS COUNTERPART OR BE STRUCK. ORDERED: an EIGHTH family in `absence-claim-aid.md` for RELATIONSHIP CLAIMS WITH NO NAMED COUNTERPART — "mirrors the TS contract", "matches the Python side", "parallels the handler" — which are worse than unverified, they are UNFALSIFIABLE, and the remedy is always identical.**

## R-320 · 2026-07-28 · AR-303 ruled: **`MANIFEST.sha256` VERIFIED 275/275 AT THE BLOB LAYER** and `* -text` proven in force — the premise I flagged as asserted-not-measured HOLDS; ★★★ **MY R-318 §1 PREMISE WAS FALSE — the root `.gitattributes` already closed that exposure, so I generalised a rule and ordered a sweep on an unverified hazard**; MINT: A RULE CAN BE RIGHT AND ITS MOTIVATING INSTANCE FALSE, and **N INSTANCES IS A CENSUS THAT OWES VERIFICATION OF EACH MEMBER**; ★★ the manifest's gap is RULED by distinguishing the two uncovered files BY KIND; the aid's scope is WIDENED — a claimed HAZARD is an absence claim about a protection

**§1 — VERIFIED, AND ON THE RIGHT FOOTING.** 275 entries · **275 MATCH · 0 MISMATCH · 0 MISSING**, hashed from `git show HEAD:<path>` — **the COMMITTED BLOB, never the working file**, which is the only reading that could have failed: a working-tree check passes even when git has normalised the stored blobs, and that is precisely the failure that hit the preservation commit. `git check-attr text` returning `unset` proves `* -text` is IN FORCE rather than merely present in a file — effect tested, not existence. ★ And the 250 stored-CRLF blobs are the point rather than a wart: they are preserved BYTE-VERBATIM as the sealed read produced them, so the manifest verifies against CRLF bytes because **the CRLF bytes are the artifact.** The premise I flagged in R-318 §1 as asserted-and-not-re-measured is now measured, and it holds.

**§2 — ★★ THE GAP IS REAL AND THE TWO UNCOVERED FILES ARE UNCOVERED FOR DIFFERENT REASONS, so they get different cures. MINTED: A GUARD WHOSE OWN PRECONDITION SITS OUTSIDE THE GUARD HAS AN UNWATCHED LOAD-BEARING WALL.** 278 tracked, 275 covered. **RULED: (i) `README.md` is EVIDENCE — it is the provenance record of irreplaceable material — so it belongs IN the manifest; add it. (ii) `.gitattributes` is a PRECONDITION, not evidence, and hashing its bytes would be the weaker cure: a same-bytes file can yield a DIFFERENT effect (a nested `.gitattributes` overriding it) and a different mechanism can yield the SAME effect, so the bytes are not what the 275 digests depend on. ASSERT THE EFFECT — `git check-attr text` unset across the manifest's paths, as part of manifest verification itself.** That is close-a-class-at-its-defining-property applied to a guard's own foundation: the property is *these paths are not eol-converted*, not *this file has these bytes*. ★ **The restraint is credited: it did not unilaterally edit an evidence manifest and asked first. That is the correct instinct around irreplaceable material, and its recommendation was the right one.**

**§3 — ★★★ MY OWN PREMISE, FALSIFIED AND OWNED. The repo root `.gitattributes` already pins `text eol=lf` repo-wide, gitattributes OVERRIDE `core.autocrlf`, and `git ls-files --eol` reports `attr/text eol=lf` on every digest subject — so AR-301's "one `core.autocrlf` away from a permanent false alarm" DESCRIBED AN EXPOSURE THAT COULD NOT OCCUR, and R-318 §1 built a generalised rule and a sweep on top of it.** Precisely what survives and what dies: **the RULE survives** — a digest over a file is stable only if the path's eol is pinned or the digest normalises, and that is now demonstrably how all 13 sites are safe; **the EXPOSURE CLAIM dies**; and so does **my class-formation** — I wrote "three instances make a class," when the honest count is ONE real instance (the preservation commit, which the repo then fixed by policy) plus one non-instance. **I assembled a class by recollection, which is the exact defect this desk has convicted three times today, committed while generalising a rule about rigour.** ★ **MINTED: A RULE CAN BE RIGHT AND ITS MOTIVATING INSTANCE FALSE — and N INSTANCES IS A CENSUS, so when I generalise from a count, each member owes verification before the count carries weight.** ★★ And the sweep is NOT waste, for a reason worth stating: **it converted an ASSUMED protection into a MEASURED one across 13 sites — including `sealed_read_driver.py:207`, the fail-closed reader-identity guard over the frozen prompts, which had it been eol-fragile would have been the R-318 §2 compound hazard in its purest form (noise × a re-freeze remedy, over irreplaceable evidence). A sweep ordered for a bad reason that returns a measured negative has still moved something from belief to knowledge.**

**§4 — ★★ THE AID'S SCOPE IS WIDENED ON THE WORKER'S OWN DIAGNOSIS, and the diagnosis is correct: A CLAIMED HAZARD IS AN ABSENCE CLAIM ABOUT A PROTECTION** ("X is exposed to Y" asserts that nothing prevents Y), **so it is the same species and settles by the same thirty-second check.** ORDERED: a seventh family in `absence-claim-aid.md` — EXPOSURE forms (`is exposed to` · `one X away from` · `could break if` · `vulnerable to` · `at risk of` · `would fail when` · `nothing prevents`) — and it runs at both desks, since R-318 §1 is my instance of it. **§5 — The sweep's result is ACCEPTED as published** (13 sites, defining property *a hash computed over bytes read from disk*, all on cure (1), two also normalising), **and the discarded RAW/NORM split is CREDITED AS THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE INSTRUMENT-OWES-A-CONTROL LAW: the classifier mislabelled the two files just normalised, so the dimension was THROWN AWAY rather than reported. A failed control does not degrade a finding's confidence — it removes that dimension from the report entirely.**

**§6 — THE ONE GENUINE DEFECT, AND IT REDEEMS THE FALSE HAZARD. `git ls-files --eol` found 4 index/worktree eol mismatches; one was the parity fixture committed in AR-300 (blob 221,833 bytes LF, working file 227,677 bytes CRLF, differing by eol only) because the generator used `write_text()` and Python translates newlines on Windows — so every regeneration re-dirtied the file against its own blob. ★ CURED AT THE SOURCE (`newline="\n"` in the generator) following THE REPO'S OWN DOCUMENTED PRECEDENT — close the source of the CRLF rather than normalise the result — and the cure BUYS A PROOF that did not exist before: regeneration is now BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed blob, so the fixture is demonstrably REPRODUCIBLE rather than merely stored, which is the artifact-staleness cure class satisfied at birth. ★★ Worth the record: A FALSE HAZARD HUNTED HONESTLY STILL FOUND A TRUE ONE — one layer over, in the reporter's own forty-minute-old commit.** The three other mismatched files (`test_spec_family_bindings.py`, `dual_denominator_remeasure.py`, `packet-session-refusal-precedence-2026-07-21.md`) are correctly named-not-touched; they ride the artifact-staleness census, cured at the SOURCE where a generator writes them and by one-time renormalisation where none does.

**§7 — Sequence:** manifest cures (§2: add `README.md`; assert the `-text` EFFECT) → make-the-excuse-assertable unit (R-319 §5) → R-317 follow-ons (publish the 18 minutes; fixture calendar dimension; flag-reach vs evidence-scope; `OVERNIGHT_END_MIN`) → aid seventh family (§4) → noisy-guard sweep → `mirrors` 661 stratum → the 66 collection floors, severity-ordered → mirror-the-logic sweep → artifact-staleness CLASS census (carrying the 3 eol mismatches) → disposition unit by species → 3-ii (+(b) migration) → 3-iii → R-304 §3 code guard → builds. **Holds:** flags OFF · FRAME HOLDS (strict floor 1) · **the irreplaceable 275 VERIFIED at the blob layer with `-text` proven in force** · corpus = 16 · 0 eligible today (honest) · the 77 sealed-and-durable · nothing live.
